name: IZEA Worldwide, Inc.
business_overview: IZEA Worldwide, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a technology-enabled influencer marketing company that connects social influencers and content creators in North America, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. The company offers IZEA Flex, its flagship platform for managing enterprise influencer marketing. It also operates marketplace that connects marketers with creators. In addition, the company offers AI-enabled tools to assist marketers and creators with text and visual content development. Additionally, it provides management of content workflow, creator search and targeting, bidding, analytics, and payment processing services. It primarily sells influencer marketing and custom content campaigns through client development team and platforms. The company was formerly known as IZEA, Inc. and changed its name to IZEA Worldwide, Inc. in August 2018. IZEA Worldwide, Inc. was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Orlando, Florida.

classification_meta.logic_summary: IZEA operates a technology-enabled influencer marketing platform connecting brands with creators, primarily through a marketplace and SaaS tools.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** IZEA is undergoing a deliberate revenue-quality pivot, exiting unprofitable SMB accounts to concentrate on enterprise clients. This shift has caused a near-term contraction in managed-services activity, but early wins with brands like Hulu and ASUS hint at re-building momentum. The launch of the AI-powered ZED platform adds a product-driven growth vector within the Creator Economy space. Overall demand visibility is muted during the transition, with the trajectory hinging on converting enterprise engagements into recurring, higher-quality bookings.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership is proactively reshaping the business model, shedding low-margin revenue while reducing costs and introducing an AI platform to differentiate the offering. A strong cash balance and zero debt support the ongoing share repurchase program, signaling confidence. The strategy emphasizes long-term profitability over top-line volume, though execution risk remains tied to the speed at which enterprise clients scale and offset the lost SMB base.

IZEA (NASDAQ: IZEA) reported Q1 2026 revenue of $6.6 million, down 18% from $8.0 million, reflecting its exit from lower-margin SMB accounts and focus on enterprise customers. Managed Services bookings were $6.3 million, down 17%.

Total costs and expenses fell 10% to $7.7 million. Net loss was $0.8 million ($0.04 per share) versus $0.1 million a year ago, while adjusted EBITDA was $(0.5) million. Cash and equivalents were $46.5 million with no long-term debt. IZEA launched its AI-powered ZED platform and added new clients including Hulu and ASUS. A $10 million stock repurchase program has used $1.3 million to buy 523,268 shares to date.
